newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Amsteel says First Asia may cost $120 mln.
newsitem.headline: Amsteel says First Asia may cost $120 mln.

text.p: Malaysian financial services company Amsteel Securities (M) Sdn Bhd said on Monday its proposed acquisition of Thai stockbrokers First Asia Securities Ltd could cost around 300 million ringgit ($120 million).
"They (First Asia) have assets of around three billion baht, so a takeover would cost us around 300 million ringgit," Amsteel managing director Lee Tak Suan said.
Lee was speaking to reporters at a news conference after a signing ceremony.
In April, Thailand's Securities One Plc said it had signed an agreement to sell First Asia Securities to a group led by Amsteel Capital Holdings Bhd.
The buying consortium is 49 percent owned by the Amsteel group, with the remainder being held by Thai partners.
Amsteel Capital Holdings is a member of the Amsteel Securities Group, which is in turn owned by Amsteel Corp Bhd.

Lee said no formal announcement would be made by Amsteel until a "due diligence" audit had been completed to ascertain the value of the company. Lee said he expected the exercise to be completed in the latter part of June. ($1=2.5 ringgit)
